steps.do: Create the two accounts the lab needs, a workspace, and put both accounts in it. Under Accounts create lena and sam (password cookbook07-lab-passphrase). In the top bar press + (Create workspace), name it and choose Create and select. Back in Administration, under Project access, pick the workspace and add lena and sam with the role Reviewer. The server must list lena in CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS and not sam.
steps.asset: accounts: lena (approver), sam (operator without the approver scope)

steps.do: Press + New Test Set, type a name, owner admin and Create; open it and press Import from file, choose ticket-cases.jsonl and press Import 44 rows. Each line's input, expected and tags become one example.
steps.see: ticket-cases.jsonl: 44 rows ready to import. then the header reads 44 active examples. A file with a bad line is refused before anything is added (Line 7 is not valid JSON.).

steps.do: Press Import, type a name, choose the file support-triage.workflow.json with Choose file, then press Validate dependencies and Import as new.
steps.see: Preflight passed, then the editor opens with classify, triage_router, draft_reply, review and action_request in the outline.

steps.do: Press Validate, then Preview, type any text and press Run Preview. Preview cannot isolate a Python Code node, so it refuses.
steps.see: The toolbar says Valid.; the preview result shows error and the step classify, whose detail reads preview cannot isolate this capability; no workflow node ran.
The toolbar says Published. (publishing creates the version; the alpha UI has no Deployments tab, so aliases are API only).

steps.do: Open Run Monitor, paste a ticket (the input object of a row of ticket-cases.jsonl) and press Run. Run TK01 (how-to), then TK29 (the bug ticket).
fill: {"ticket_text": "How do I enable SSO for my workspace? I just want the steps.", "channel": "chat", "customer_tier": "free"}
the export-button 500 in production ticket, tier pro, account acct_2101
steps.see: TK01 reaches completed. TK29 stops at waiting_approval with Approve and Reject buttons.

steps.do: As the same account that started the run, press Approve.
steps.see: Approve failed: the account that triggered this run cannot approve it; a second person must decide and the run stays at waiting_approval.

steps.do: Sign in as lena in another browser profile, choose the workspace in the top bar, open Workflows, the workflow and its Runs tab. Select the run that shows Awaiting approval, press Approve, then Resume.
steps.see: The run shows Completed; its output starts with APPROVED_ACTION.

steps.where: Workflows › Run Monitor, then Runs as lena
steps.do: As admin run the refund ticket TK40 (I was charged twice for October); it pauses at the gate. As sam (an operator without the approver scope) open it on the Runs tab and press Approve: refused for the missing caliber.approver scope. As lena press Reject.
steps.see: sam is refused; the run shows Failed after lena rejects and never reaches action_request: nothing is released.
The newest approval row is by lena; the enqueue rows are by admin.

steps.do: On Versions press Restore as draft on v1: a new editable draft (v2) opens. Double-click classify in the outline and, in the inspector's Python code, change urgent_markers = has([ to urgent_markers = False and has([. Save, Validate, open Run Monitor and run TK29 again; on the workflow's Runs tab select that run and open its classify step. Back in the editor Publish (v2); on Versions pick v1 as Base (older) and v2 as Compare (newer).
steps.see: The classify output now says "severity": "medium" (v1: "high"). The comparison shows exactly one modified node, classify.

steps.do: Press Restore as draft on v1 again (v3), run TK29, open the classify step on the Runs tab, then Publish. Moving a staging alias back is API only in this alpha UI.
steps.see: "severity": "high" again; Versions lists v1, v2 and v3.
